newsitem.title: USA: Forest Labs seen lower after loss forecast.
newsitem.headline: Forest Labs seen lower after loss forecast.

text.p: Forest Laboratories Inc shares were indicated to open at 30-34, sharply down from Tuesday's 38-3/4 close, after the company forecast operating losses for the next two quarters and for all of fiscal 1997.
Morgan Stanley said it downgraded the stock to neutral from outperform.

The pharmaceutical manufacturer and marketer late Tuesday said it had decided to eliminate trade incentives for all of its branded products to reduce high trade inventory levels, principally of Aerobid, its inhaled steroid product used in treating asthma.

"This action will result in reduced sales over the remaining two quarters of the fiscal year ending March 31, 1997, and possibly the first quarter of fiscal 1998, and operating losses for the next two quarters and for all of fiscal 1997," Forest said.

The company previously said it planned to reduce its trade inventory gradually. On Tuesday, It said it had decided to substantially reduce the high inventory levels due to the decline in Aerobid's growth rate.
The Morgan analyst was not available for details.
Lehman analyst Richard Silver said he cut his fiscal 1997 estimate on Forest to a loss of $0.77 a share from a profit of $1.28, and cut his fiscal 1998 estimate to $1.90 from $2.40.
Silver, in a report, maintained his outperform rating on the stock and recommended that long-term investors "buy on a downdraft."
Silver noted that Aerobid is Forest's flagship inhaled steroid for asthma.
Later, Forest shares were indicated to open even lower, in a range of 26-30.
